propositions: An errored side of a paired parity run carries a synthetic decision ("dropped") never produced by the model, but decision_flips comparison at parity.py:107 treats it as a real verdict, scoring it as a flip when it differs from the other arm's actual decision.

A single transient throttle exception on one arm fails the parity gating criterion (b) with a fabricated decision flip, even though criterion (d) separately gates runtime error rate, causing double-counting and false quality regressions.

The errored field is not guarded in the decision_flips comprehension (parity.py:107) despite being documented at parity.py:46 as "not a model verdict", allowing pairs where either side errored to be scored as flips.

Gold pair filtering at parity.py:105 tests the gold label, not the decision field, so no decision-vocabulary membership test can exclude errored pairs from decision_flips; discriminating experiment proved decision="__error__" outside _DECISIONS was still counted as a flip.

Reports from arms with different combinations of real flips and errors (e.g., 3 real+0 errors vs 2 real+1 error vs 0 real+3 errors) all produce byte-identical gating strings with no per-pair detail, making fabricated flips indistinguishable from real ones.
An errored=True, valid=True record silently produces a fabricated flip with no corroborating signal in validity or error_rate metrics, leaving the defect completely undetectable.
